text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare provider. In the absence of clear symptoms, an abnormal test result is typically repeated on a second day to confirm the diagnosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests evaluated by a healthcare provider

text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed when any of the following thresholds are met, according to guidelines from the American Diabetes Association:

list.snippet: Hemoglobin A1C Test (HbA1c): 6.5% or higher (measures average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months).
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher (after fasting for at least 8 hours).
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher (measured 2 hours after drinking a 75-gram glucose solution).

Random Plasma Glucose Test: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher (tested anytime in someone who is experiencing classic symptoms of high blood sugar like frequent urination, extreme thirst, or unexplained weight loss).

text_blocks.snippet: Before type 2 diabetes develops, blood sugar levels are often elevated but not high enough to meet the diabetes threshold:

list.snippet: Fasting Blood Glucose: 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L)

text_blocks.snippet: More detailed information and screening guidance can be found through MedlinePlus or Mayo Clinic.
